newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mercedes expects higher sales, profits.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes expects higher sales, profits.

text.p: Mercedes-Benz AG said on Friday that it expected sales of its cars and trucks to growth this year, ensuring higher profits.
The company, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, said in a statement it expected sales to climb to 77 billion marks from 72.03 billion marks the year before.
Mercedes said it expected 1996 car deliveries of more than 640,000 units, up from 590,200 the year before. Truck deliveries, meanwhile, should climb to 345,000 units from 320,089.
Mercedes also said it expected record sales and deliveries of its cars and truck in 1997 and that its business outlook was separate from the overall economy.

Detailing the sales figures for 1996, Mercedes said car sales would climb to 46 billion marks from 40.4 billion marks and that truck sales would remain steady around 31 billion marks compared with 31.6 billion marks the year before.
The forecasts and figures were broadly in line with previous statements from the company.
Mercedes said car sales were driven largely by its E-class model and strong demand for its SLK sports car.
The car maker said it intended to increase production of the two-seat cabriolet SLK in 1997 to 47,000 units from an originally planned 35,000.
